problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}5 & 20 & -10 & -5 \\ -2 & -8 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & 12\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.

examples.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination with Row Exchanges
examples.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\begin{aligned} & x+y+z=-2 \\  & x+y+2z=-1 \\  & x+2y+z=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
examples.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get $a_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\begin{aligned}x+y+z=-2 \\ y=3 \\ z=1,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=1$ tells us the value of $z,$ and the second equation $y=3$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting these values into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+(3)+(1)=-2\,⟹\,x=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-6,$ $y=3,$ and $z=1.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -6,3,1 \rangle.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+2z=-3 \\  & x+2y+2z=2 \\  & 3x+4y+4z=8\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and hence solve the linear system.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 4 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & 4 & 4 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 17\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+2z=-3 \\  & y=5 \\  & z=-6\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. Substituting both $y=5$ and $z=-6$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x+5+2(-6)=-3\,⟹\,x-7=-3\,⟹\,x=4.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=4,$ $y=5,$ and $z=-6.$
